title: SOS doesn’t stand for ‘save our souls’, or for anything at all
body: SOS was chosen as a sound pattern, not a phrase: three dots, three dashes and three dots, sent as one unbroken signal that is hard to mistake, even through static. Germany adopted it in 1905, and the first International Radiotelegraph Convention made it the worldwide standard from 1908. ‘Save our souls’ and ‘save our ship’ are backronyms, invented later to fit the letters.
